posts.text: One of the few general rules in ecology is that biodiversity increases as you approach the equator. But there’s an exception. The global latitudinal diversity gradient for birds is three times weaker in cities than in natural areas. In PNAS: https://ow.ly/9xmR50ZFVLZ

posts.text: A deep dive into the capacity for trees to physiologically adapt to drought reaches a sobering conclusion: Trees have little ability to change their inner hydraulic systems to accommodate increasing levels of drought as the climate changes. In PNAS: https://ow.ly/rcBR50ZFVIC

posts.text: Antimicrobial-resistant bacteria and associated genes lurk in farm soil, but field experiments show that switching from industrial monocultures to less-intensive, low-input systems with diverse crop rotations can mitigate the threat. In PNAS: https://ow.ly/HN0r50ZFVHw

posts.text: Old-growth grasslands are slow to recover once destroyed. Characteristic plants of such grasslands are shorter and have smaller leaves with less nitrogen than plants in secondary grasslands, which are resource-acquisitive and more competitive. In PNAS: https://ow.ly/zOl950ZFVFu
